panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Top-left overview of left posterior neck showing erythematous papules in serpiginous pattern before treatment in biopsy-confirmed EPS case; article titled Pulse Dye Laser Therapy Successful for Elastosis Perforans Serpiginosa. B: Top-right overview of right posterior neck showing annular/serpiginous erythematous papules before treatment in biopsy-confirmed EPS case. C: Bottom-left close-up of left neck lesions showing erythematous umbilicated/keratotic papules in serpiginous arrangement, biopsy-confirmed EPS. D: Bottom-right close-up of right neck lesions showing erythematous keratotic papules in serpiginous/annular pattern, biopsy-confirmed EPS.
panels.attribution_text: Rinaldi et al. Pulse Dye Laser Therapy Successful for Elastosis Perforans Serpiginosa.. Case reports in dermatological medicine 2019. doi:10.1155/2019/2860746. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Lesions on left & right neck before treatment.
in_text_mentions: On examination, he had two localized areas of erythematous umbilicated papules arranged in a serpiginous pattern on both the left and right side of his posterior neck (Figure 1). A biopsy had been performed at his previous centre of care and a diagnosis of EPS was confirmed. An EPS biopsy, as shown on DermNet.nz, shows keratotic debris columns perforating through a hyperplastic epidermis. This can be accentuated using an Elastic-Van Gieson stain that highlights elastic fibres in black (Figure 2) [5].

findings.label: Transepidermal elimination channels
findings.evidence: transepidermal elimination of basophilic debris, neutrophils and brightly eosinophilic collagen fibres

panels.rationale: H&E punch biopsy from left upper back with caption-stated transepidermal elimination of debris and eosinophilic fibres, explicitly stated as consistent with elastosis perforans serpiginosa in a patient with coexisting EPS and acquired cutis laxa. Histology shows perforation channel, matching vocabulary finding.
panels.attribution_text: Ma and Van Rooij. Coexisting elastosis perforans serpiginosa and acquired cutis laxa following long-term penicillamine in Wilson disease.. Skin health and disease 2025. doi:10.1093/skinhd/vzaf060. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Left upper back punch biopsy stained with haematoxylin and eosin at ×100 magnification. The staining shows multiple foci with transepidermal elimination of basophilic debris, neutrophils and brightly eosinophilic collagen fibres, associated with hyperplastic squamous epithelium. These findings are consistent with elastosis perforans serpiginosa.
in_text_mentions: Punch biopsy revealed hyperplastic epithelium with trans­epidermal elimination of basophilic debris, neutrophils and brightly eosinophilic collagen fibres (Figure 3). Verhoeff-Van Gieson staining demonstrated thickened, serrated elastin fibres, confirming EPS (Figure 4).
